one_line_contribution: On ALFWorld's search-bound task types, a ~300-token rule-compiled object-to-receptacle frequency table (a cross-episode aggregate no set of k retrieved trajectories contains) placed as a cached static prefix matches or beats k=3 retrieval at zero uncached prefill, with a depth-at-fixed-coverage ladder, a token-matched deranged table, a no-experience LLM-written table, and a whole-bank-with-and-without-its-own-table pair attributing the gain to aggregation of experience rather than coverage, scaffold, or pretraining.
closest_prior_work: Verified (literature command, S2+HF): arXiv 2607.00022 PerSim, 'When to Personalize Household Object Search: A Rigidity-Gated Hybrid Policy' (2026-06-18) — it uses population-frequency object-placement priors as the baseline policy for household object search and asks when trait-conditioned priors add over them; the mechanism the proposal wants to demonstrate (aggregated placement frequencies drive search efficiency) is its premise, not its finding. It does not threaten the specific contrast here (its priors are learned for a robot search policy, not an in-context artifact for an LLM reader, and it has no retrieval-of-raw-episodes arm at matched tokens), but it does mean the mechanism is not the novelty. Same for verified 2603.05642 (SymSearch: LLM relational knowledge distilled offline into lightweight models for interactive object search) and, older, 2302.12915 (S^4, LLM semantic spatial distributions for object search) and 2207.10761 (TIDEE, visuo-semantic commonsense placement priors) — both retrieved by my home-vocabulary query. On the method side the closest is verified 2504.07952 Dynamic Cheatsheet (2025-04, EACL, 113 citations): a compiled, persistently accumulated in-context artifact from experience; it never contrasts the compiled artifact with retrieval of the raw episodes and never varies how much experience is compiled, which is exactly the gap this proposal fills, so it constrains novelty to the attribution design rather than to the artifact. Net: what is new here is the placebo-controlled attribution of a compiled artifact's gain against a retrieval baseline at matched tokens, not the artifact or the mechanism.
strongest_objection: The study is scoped to the cell where the claim is cheapest, and the one contrast that carries the title's weight is one the authors themselves expect to come out null. (a) Cell S is precisely where Measurement A found retrieval weakest — look-at-in-light is -4.8 (retrieval hurts), pick types +15/+18, versus +39..+55 on clean/heat/cool — so M1=+10 is a pooled target that averages in a negative component, and the +20..+27 procedure-bound residual, which is the bulk of what retrieval actually buys on this node, is declared out of scope up front. 'What retrieval cannot carry' therefore turns out to be a small slice of what retrieval does carry. (b) P4 (cheatsheet_all - LLM-prior >= +7) is the load-bearing test of 'compiled from the bank', and the proposal concedes the null is plausible because ALFWorld placements are stereotyped; if a Qwen3-32B-authored table in the same format matches the compiled one, the paper's title claim is false and the result collapses to 'put an object-location table in the prompt', which robotics established years ago (2207.10761, 2302.12915) and which 2607.00022 uses as a baseline. (c) The automated entailment check is right that P3 and P7 are near-entailed by P1 and that P8's drift gate cannot fail (its band equals the 268-cell floor, and all three k3-k0 branches end in 'proceed'), so of eight predictions only P2, P4, P6 and the P5 additivity question carry independent information — on one environment and one backbone. An AC will ask what the paper says if P4 is null, and the honest answer ('informative negative for the area') is a workshop-sized result.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Promote P4 to the headline: the interesting question is not whether a location table helps (robotics says yes) but whether compiling it from 1,465 trajectories beats what a 32B model already believes, and the pre-registered top-1 row agreement covariate makes that a real study; state the paper's contribution as the compiled-vs-parametric-vs-retrieved triangle so a null on any leg is still a result. (2) Test 'retrieval cannot aggregate' against a retriever that could: add an object-conditioned retrieval arm (retrieve the k trajectories containing the goal's object class, rather than by goal sentence, which on six templates returns same-type trajectories) and a fresh k=7/k=15 arm at 8 seeds; if a k=7 object-keyed retriever recovers the same gain, the structural claim is wrong and the paper is about token cost, not about what retrieval can carry. (3) Repair the three entailment defects the automated check names: score P3 at M1 plus the measured shuffled_all - k0 gap (or as an equivalence-to-k0 test), make the both-arms-take restricted version of P7 primary or score it within the succeeded-in-both stratum, and set P8's band from paired same-arm re-run noise (~+-6) with one k3-k0 branch that actually stops the run. (4) Manipulate the search-bound property instead of naming it, as the round's binding rule demands: build a variant bank/task set in which a subset of object classes is given a deliberately flat or scene-specific placement distribution, so 'the statistic helps only where search is the bottleneck and the prior is concentrated' becomes a two-level manipulation on one environment rather than a 2-seed exploratory contrast.
missing_baseline: Two, both cheap. (i) Object-conditioned retrieval: every retrieval arm here is keyed on the goal sentence (k3, k7), which on a six-template benchmark returns same-type trajectories and therefore almost never carries multiple observed placements of the target object; a retriever keyed on the object class named in the goal would put 3-7 real placements of that exact object in context and is the fair opponent for the claim that per-query retrieval 'structurally cannot' aggregate. Without it the finding is about one retriever, not about retrieval. (ii) A marginal-only receptacle-frequency list — the top receptacles overall with no object conditioning, token-matched — to separate 'the agent needs the conditional distribution P(receptacle | object)' from 'the agent just needs a good default search order'. shuffled_all is a wrong-content placebo, not a base-rate control, and on ALFWorld a bare 'check countertop, drawer, cabinet, fridge first' instruction could plausibly capture most of a +10 effect; if it does, the cross-episode-aggregate framing loses its point.

NOT verified: the 'WCCIS 2026' paper the proposal names as its nearest overlap — it has no arXiv id and a title query returned nothing on either channel, so the submission's central reassurance ('the nearest overlap motivates rather than tests the claim') cannot be checked by a reviewer; also unverified are 2602.06459 UcON, 2606.05684 and 2511.20857 (cited only in passing). Judging the check itself: it is better than most in this round — three query classes, IDs reported, a genuine home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words, and an honest empty result reported as empty. Two weaknesses. Its queries are uniformly placement- or cheatsheet-flavored and therefore miss the compiled-vs-raw memory literature that is the real competitor for its framing: 2605.12978 ('preserving raw episodic trajectories maintains better accuracy' than LLM-consolidated memory) and 2605.18421 EvoMemBench ('long-context baselines continue to outperform specialized memory methods') both bear directly on the Related Work assertion that whole-bank and compiled controls are not run, and the second partially pre-empts the brief's G3/G12/G17 gap. And the check's 'no pre-emption' verdict is scored on the narrow compiled-statistic-vs-retrieval comparison, which is indeed unrun, while acknowledging that the underlying mechanism is established in robotics and then treating that as confirmation; a skeptical AC reads the same fact as a novelty cost, which is where I have scored it.
